chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, from Ibn Miskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked him about a man and a woman praying in one house, while the woman is on the right side of the man, parallel with him. He said: No, unless there is between them a handspan or a cubit.

Then he said: The length of the saddle-pack of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was a cubit, and he would place it in front of himself when he performed salat, so that it would screen him from one who might pass in front of him.

key_terms.بِحِذَائِهِ: directly parallel to him, at his side
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: a cubit as a measure of separation
key_terms.رَحْلِ: saddle-pack or saddle equipment used here as a physical barrier
key_terms.شِبْرٌ: a handspan as a measure of separation
key_terms.لِيَسْتُرَهُ: to screen or cover him from passersby during salat

ai.seo_question: Can a man and a woman pray side by side in the same room in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a man and a woman performing salat in the same place while standing side by side. It states that this is not permitted unless there is a separating distance of at least a handspan or a cubit, and it supports this with the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم using a barrier in front of himself during salat.
